front: Older man with nocturia, weak stream and a smooth enlarged prostate: first-line drug, when to add a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor, and PSA screening ages?
bottom: Alpha-blocker first; add 5-ARI if the prostate is enlarged.

bullets.clue: Smooth, symmetric, enlarged prostate; nocturia, hesitancy, weak stream.
bullets.treat: Tamsulosin works in days; finasteride shrinks the gland over months.
bullets.trap: PSA screening: shared decision at ages 55–69.

back: Alpha-blocker first; add 5-ARI if the prostate is enlarged. Key clue: Smooth, symmetric, enlarged prostate; nocturia, hesitancy, weak stream. First-line: Tamsulosin works in days; finasteride shrinks the gland over months. Exam trap: PSA screening: shared decision at ages 55–69.

diagram.alt: Benign prostatic hyperplasia: smooth enlarged prostate with obstructive symptoms; alpha-blocker first, add a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor for large glands.

source.guideline: AUA Guideline: Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to BPH (2023 amendment); USPSTF Prostate Cancer Screening
source.recommendation: AUA 2023: alpha-blockers (e.g., tamsulosin) and 5-ARIs for LUTS/BPH; 5-ARIs are for enlarged prostate. USPSTF 2018 (grade C): men 55–69 individual decision after discussion; grade D at 70+.

front: Leaks with cough or sneeze, versus sudden urgency, versus constant dribbling with a distended bladder: which type, and first-line management?
bottom: Stress, urgency (OAB) and overflow incontinence: treat each differently.

bullets.clue: Stress: leak with cough. Urge: can't make it. Overflow: dribble, residual urine.
bullets.treat: Stress: pelvic floor training. Urge: bladder training, then drug.
bullets.trap: Check post-void residual: antimuscarinics worsen retention.

back: Stress, urgency (OAB) and overflow incontinence: treat each differently. Key clue: Stress: leak with cough. Urge: can't make it. Overflow: dribble, residual urine. First-line: Stress: pelvic floor training. Urge: bladder training, then drug. Exam trap: Check post-void residual: antimuscarinics worsen retention.

diagram.alt: Incontinence types: stress leaks with cough, urge has sudden urgency and is treated with bladder training and drugs, overflow dribbles with a high post-void residual.

source.guideline: AUA/SUFU Guideline on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Idiopathic Overactive Bladder
source.recommendation: AUA/SUFU 2024 OAB: behavioral therapies, antimuscarinics or β3-agonists as non-surgical options (no longer labeled 'first-line'); AUA/SUFU SUI 2017, amended 2023: counsel on observation, PFMT ± biofeedback, other options and surgery.

task_area: History Taking and Performing Physical Examination
front: Acute scrotum exam: what do the cremasteric reflex, Prehn sign, transillumination and a 'bag of worms' tell you?
bottom: Absent cremasteric reflex suggests torsion; light shines through a hydrocele.

bullets.clue: Torsion: high-riding, horizontal testis. Varicocele: bag of worms.
bullets.treat: Epididymitis: ceftriaxone plus doxycycline. Torsion: urgent surgery.
bullets.trap: Prehn sign is unreliable: don't use it to exclude torsion.

back: Absent cremasteric reflex suggests torsion; light shines through a hydrocele. Key clue: Torsion: high-riding, horizontal testis. Varicocele: bag of worms. First-line: Epididymitis: ceftriaxone plus doxycycline. Torsion: urgent surgery. Exam trap: Prehn sign is unreliable: don't use it to exclude torsion.

diagram.alt: Scrotal exam: absent cremasteric reflex suggests torsion, hydrocele transilluminates, varicocele feels like a bag of worms; epididymitis is treated with ceftriaxone and doxycycline.

source.guideline: CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines: Epididymitis; AUA Acute Scrotum curriculum
source.recommendation: CDC 2021: epididymitis, likely chlamydia/gonorrhea: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once plus doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 10 days; enteric organisms in insertive anal sex or older men: add levofloxacin-based regimen. Torsion: urgent surgery (see pance-016).

front: Painless firm testicular mass in a 25-year-old with a history of cryptorchidism: first test, tumor markers, and surgery? Why not biopsy?

bullets.clue: Painless solid intratesticular mass; ↑AFP, hCG or LDH.
bullets.treat: Scrotal ultrasound, markers, then radical inguinal orchiectomy.
bullets.trap: No transscrotal biopsy: it alters lymphatic spread.

back: Testicular cancer until proven otherwise. Key clue: Painless solid intratesticular mass; ↑AFP, hCG or LDH. First-line: Scrotal ultrasound, markers, then radical inguinal orchiectomy. Exam trap: No transscrotal biopsy: it alters lymphatic spread.

diagram.alt: Testicular cancer: painless solid testicular mass; scrotal ultrasound and tumor markers AFP, hCG and LDH, then radical inguinal orchiectomy; avoid scrotal biopsy.

source.guideline: AUA Guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Early-Stage Testicular Cancer (2023 amendment)
source.recommendation: AUA 2019/2023: scrotal ultrasound for suspected mass; serum AFP, hCG and LDH; radical inguinal orchiectomy for suspected testicular cancer; avoid transscrotal procedures.

front: Painless gross hematuria in a 65-year-old smoker: what is the likely diagnosis and work-up? What is the classic renal cell carcinoma presentation?

bullets.clue: Painless gross hematuria; smoking is the main risk. RCC: hematuria, flank pain, flank mass.
bullets.trap: Anticoagulants don't explain hematuria: still evaluate.

back: Bladder (urothelial) cancer until proven otherwise. Key clue: Painless gross hematuria; smoking is the main risk. RCC: hematuria, flank pain, flank mass. First-line: Cystoscopy plus upper-tract imaging (CT urography). Exam trap: Anticoagulants don't explain hematuria: still evaluate.

diagram.alt: Painless gross hematuria in an older smoker suggests bladder cancer; evaluate with cystoscopy and CT urography; renal cell carcinoma classically presents with hematuria, flank pain and a flank mass (triad, uncommon).

source.recommendation: AUA/SUFU 2025: hematuria risk stratification; cystoscopy and upper-tract imaging for high-risk patients; gross hematuria warrants evaluation.

front: Why can a nitrate plus a PDE-5 inhibitor drop blood pressure?
bottom: Both raise cGMP in vascular smooth muscle, so the effect stacks.

bullets.clue: Nitric oxide activates guanylate cyclase. PDE-5 breaks cGMP down.
bullets.treat: Do not combine nitrates with sildenafil, tadalafil, or vardenafil.
bullets.trap: The washout depends on which PDE-5 inhibitor was taken.

back: Both raise cGMP in vascular smooth muscle, so the effect stacks. Key clue: Nitric oxide activates guanylate cyclase. PDE-5 breaks cGMP down. First-line: Do not combine nitrates with sildenafil, tadalafil, or vardenafil. Exam trap: The washout depends on which PDE-5 inhibitor was taken.

diagram.alt: Both raise cGMP in vascular smooth muscle, so the effect stacks.

source.guideline: FDA Prescribing Information for PDE-5 inhibitors
source.recommendation: Princeton IV 2024: ED is a marker of cardiovascular risk; PDE-5 inhibitors appropriate with CV stability; nitrates contraindicated (24 h sildenafil/vardenafil, 48 h tadalafil).

task_area: History Taking and Performing Physical Examination
front: Fever, dysuria and perineal pain with a tender, boggy prostate: diagnosis, what exam step to avoid, and treatment length?
bottom: Acute bacterial prostatitis: culture, then weeks of antibiotics.

bullets.clue: Fever, irritative voiding, tender, swollen, boggy prostate.
bullets.treat: Urine culture first; IV broad-spectrum if ill, then oral for 2–4 weeks.
bullets.trap: No prostatic massage: it can cause bacteremia.

back: Acute bacterial prostatitis: culture, then weeks of antibiotics. Key clue: Fever, irritative voiding, tender, swollen, boggy prostate. First-line: Urine culture first; IV broad-spectrum if ill, then oral for 2–4 weeks. Exam trap: No prostatic massage: it can cause bacteremia.

diagram.alt: Acute bacterial prostatitis: fever and a tender boggy prostate; do not massage; urine culture then antibiotics for two to four weeks.

source.recommendation: EAU: acute bacterial prostatitis: urine culture, broad-spectrum parenteral antibiotics if severe, oral therapy; total duration 2–4 weeks; AAFP review cross-check.
